To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) syngeneic transplantation in newborn MPS VII animals prevents hearing loss, 2) the transplanted animals have normal hearing until they are 11 weeks of age, 3) the transplated animals develop some degree of hearing loss by 33 weeks but it is less severe than in untreated mutants, 4) treated animals have beta-glucuronase-positive cells in temporal bone, 5) treated animals have less thickening of middle ear mucosa, 6
syngeneically transplanted MPSVII mice have improved auditory function and that this improvement is associated with a reduction in the pathology of the middle ear and cochlea.
syngeneically transplanted MPS mice have less hearing loss than non-transplanted MPS mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of gene transfer techniques to treat lysosomal storage disorders.
the development and characterization of animal models of human genetic diseases.
the development of gene therapy for lysosomal storage disorders and with the development of a mouse model of mucopolysac-charidosis type VII for testing new therapies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the BMT procedure in the MPS VII model is a very useful model for the study of auditory function in lysosomal storage diseases and that it may be a useful treatment for the auditory impairment in these disorders.
syngenei BMT in newborn mice prevents the early hearing loss and results in long term improved auditory function in the MPS VII mice.
the auditory system of MPS VII mice is a target for the lysosomal storage disease and that BMT is an effective therapy for this disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
syngeneically transplanted MPS VIIs have improved hearing, less storage in the cochlear bone, less storage in their middle ears, and less storage in the external auditory canal.
BMT is an important tool to treat lysosomal storage diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMT is a viable option for the treatment of MPS VII and other lysosomal storage diseases.
BMT in the newborn MPS VII mouse prevents the early hearing loss and in some animals results in long-term, improved auditory function.
